Overview

The Salesforce Certified Service Cloud Consultant exam validates your ability to design and implement Service Cloud solutions that meet business requirements. This guide provides the most current exam facts, a comprehensive study plan, domain breakdown, and strategies for tackling the scenario-based questions that dominate the exam.

This guide is your final preparation resource before taking the Salesforce Certified Service Cloud Consultant (CRT-150 / SC2) exam.

Exam Facts

Current Exam Structure

DetailValue
Exam NameSalesforce Certified Agentforce Service Consultant (formerly Service Cloud Consultant)
Exam CodeCRT-150 (SC2)
Number of Questions60 scored + up to 5 unscored
Time Limit105 minutes
Passing Score78% (English); 67% (Japanese)
Exam Fee$200 (plus applicable taxes)
Retake Fee$100 (plus applicable taxes)
PrerequisiteSalesforce Certified Platform Administrator
FormatMultiple choice, multiple-select, scenario-based
DeliveryOnline proctored or in-person test center

Exam Domains and Weights

As of Spring '26, Case Management alone is 32% of the exam — master it first. Combined, the top three sections (Case Management, Service Cloud Platform, Interaction Channels) are 56%.

DomainWeightFocus Areas
Case Management32%Case lifecycle, queues, assignment rules, escalation rules, auto-response rules, case teams, email-to-case, web-to-case
Service Cloud Platform13%Service Cloud configuration, Lightning console apps, macros, quick text, Einstein features, entitlements & milestones
Interaction Channels11%Email-to-case, web-to-case, live chat, messaging, voice (CTI), social customer service, self-service portals
Knowledge Management10%Knowledge article types, data categories, article visibility, Knowledge in Service Console, Lightning Knowledge
Contact Center Analytics9%Case reports, service dashboards, SLA adherence reporting, agent productivity metrics
Service Cloud Solution Design9%Gathering requirements, matching business needs to features, ROI and business case scenarios
Integrations and Data Management8%CTI integration, third-party telephony, data migration for cases/contacts, external data sources
Service Console8%Console navigation, split view, workspace tabs, subtabs, macros, keyboard shortcuts, utility bar

Tips for Scenario-Based Questions

Scenario Analysis Framework

Read the scenario carefully and identify:

  1. Business requirements: What is the customer trying to accomplish?
  2. Constraints: What limitations exist (licenses, editions, budget)?
  3. Pain points: What problems is the current system causing?
  4. Success criteria: What does success look like?
  5. Architectural debt: What existing systems must be preserved?

Analyze answer choices:

  1. Does the answer address ALL the requirements?
  2. Does the answer respect ALL the constraints?
  3. Does the answer address the ROOT cause or just a symptom?
  4. Is the answer the most EFFICIENT use of the platform?
  5. Does the answer align with Salesforce best practices?

Common Scenario Patterns

PatternBest Answer Strategy
High case volumeRecommend Omni-Channel + automation
SLA compliance issuesRecommend entitlements + milestones
Agent productivityRecommend console + macros + quick text
Knowledge gapsRecommend Knowledge + article suggestions
Multi-channel supportRecommend unified channel configuration
Data migrationRecommend phased migration + validation
Integration needsRecommend API-based solutions

Speed Reading Technique

  1. Read the last paragraph first (question stem)
  2. Scan scenario for constraints (editions, licenses, numbers)
  3. Identify the decision point (what action is required)
  4. Evaluate each answer against requirements
  5. Eliminate impossible answers (license/schema violations)
  6. Choose the BEST fit (not just a valid answer)

Exam-Taking Strategies

StrategyDescription
Time Management~1.5 minutes per question, save time for review
FlaggingFlag uncertain questions and return later
Process of EliminationEliminate obvious wrong answers first
Don't OverthinkYour first instinct is usually correct
Watch for TrapsSimilar-sounding but different options
Manage FatigueTake structured breaks if needed

Before the Exam

  1. Confirm the exam date, time, and location
  2. Test your environment (online proctoring)
  3. Have a quiet, well-lit space
  4. Keep water and snacks nearby
  5. Get a good night's sleep
  6. Arrive 15-30 minutes early

During the Exam

  1. Read every question carefully
  2. Look for "NOT" and "EXCEPT" keywords
  3. Consider all requirements before answering
  4. Use process of elimination
  5. Flag difficult questions and return later
  6. Save at least 15 minutes for review

Hands-On Tasks

  1. Create Study Schedule: Set up your 6-week study plan
  2. Build Practice Scenario Questions: Write 10 scenario questions
  3. Complete Sandbox Exercises: Do all exercises from guide 14
  4. Take Mock Exams: Complete practice test and review misses
  5. Review Use Cases: Work through all three capstone projects
  6. Time Your Study: Practice answering questions in exam time limits
  7. Assess Weak Areas: Identify and review low-score domains

Self-Check Questions

  1. What is the passing score for the English version of the exam?
  2. Which domain carries the highest weight?
  3. How many questions are on the exam (including unscored)?
  4. What is the prerequisite certification for Service Cloud Consultant?
  5. What is the exam fee?
  6. How much time do you have to complete the exam?

Common Exam Traps

  • Trap: Choosing the "possible" answer instead of the "best" answer.
  • Trap: Missing "NOT" or "EXCEPT" in the question stem.
  • Trap: Selecting answers that violate license or edition constraints.
  • Trap: Choosing answers that solve one problem but create another.
  • Trap: Rushing through scenario questions without reading closely.
  • Trap: Forgetting that hardware/appliance solutions are not the best fit for cloud-first customers.
  • Trap: Assuming all integration tools are interchangeable — REST API vs. Flow vs. Connect-Custom tools have distinct uses.
